thread.title: Silicon Valley stocks hammered again as Dow plunges 1,000 points

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Silicon Valley stocks hammered again as Dow plunges 1,000 points

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high technology index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 8, 2018, 1:40pm PST Updated Feb 8, 2018, 2:34pm PST Silicon Valley's biggest stocks plunged Thursday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,032 points and the S&P 500 dropped 3.7 percent. The stock market has been in turmoil this week as investors fret about the prospect of rising inflation and interest rates. The Dow is now down 10 percent from its high and the S&P closed at a low for the week. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index , an index of the region's largest technology stocks, dropped 3.88 percent as all 13 of its members slumped. The biggest decline came from HP Inc (NYSE: HPQ) , down 6.08 percent. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) fell 6.04 percent. Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC) dropped 5.42 percent. Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) slipped 4.77 percent and Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) dropped 4.52 percent. Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL) and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) were down 4.15 percent and 3.89 percent, respectively. Even the best performer on the index, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), ended the day firmly in the red, closing down 2.27 percent. Among all Silicon Valley stocks, Coherent (NASDAQ: COHR) fell the most. The Santa Clara-based laser systems maker plummeted 17.36 percent after it offered up a weak quarterly profit outlook . Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) shares dropped 8.63 percent the day after reporting its biggest-ever quarterly loss . Investors apparently weren't soothed by CEO Elon Musk 's projections of slowing cash burn this year. ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) fell 8.53 percent. The company may be experiencing an overdue correction: Until now, it's been largely unscathed by the stock market tumult. Few Silicon Valley stocks closed the day in the green, but Sunnyvale-based Infinera Corp. (NASDAQ: INFN) soared 29.86 percent after beating quarterly earnings expectations and on a bullish analyst outlook. Shares of the fiber optic equipment maker have “the raw material ... in terms of market growth, new products, and a renewed focus on sales and new product execution” to move into the "double digits," analyst Tim Savageaux of Northland Capital, said, according to Barron's . Savageaux raised his rating on Infinera stock from "market perform" to "outperform" with an $11 price target. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 8, 2018, 1:40pm PST Updated Feb 8, 2018, 2:34pm PST Related Content
